title: Meet the friends

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Hello! I am Sara. Taylor and Evan are my parents.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I am a chef. Clarice is my friend. She is a fashion designer.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: I am a financial analyst. I work with numbers.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I design clothes. These are my sketches.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Maria and I are roommates. I am a teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: I am a counselor. Our friend Ethan is an anesthesiologist.

reading: Sara is a student. Taylor and Evan are her parents. Taylor is a chef, and Evan is a financial analyst. Clarice is Taylor’s friend. She is a fashion designer. Denali is a teacher, and Maria is a counselor. They are roommates. Ethan is an anesthesiologist. These people have different jobs, but they are part of the same circle of friends. We will follow their everyday lives.
task: Introduce two characters. Replace their names with subject pronouns, then write a sentence using an object pronoun.

title: A visit to Chicago

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: Is your flight to Chicago today?

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Yes. I am at the airport. My father lives in Chicago.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: How long is your visit?

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Five days and four nights. There is one suitcase with me.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: Are there any books in your bag?

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Yes, there are two books and a gift for my father. My ID and boarding pass are ready.

reading: Denali is at the airport. Her flight is from Omaha to Chicago. Her father lives in Chicago, and her visit is five days and four nights long. There is one suitcase beside her. There are two books and a gift in her bag. Her ID and boarding pass are ready. Maria is at home. She sends Denali a message before the flight.

questions.prompt: How many books are in the bag?

focus: Nouns, plurals and there is / there are
task: Describe Denali’s bag with there is and there are. Include one singular and two plural nouns.

title: The missing keys

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Excuse me. Are these your keys?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes, they are! Thank you. I often put them in this pocket.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: I am Ethan. Do you live near this grocery store?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes. I am Clarice. I also work nearby. I design clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: That sounds interesting. I work at the hospital.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Please tell me about your work. And thanks again for the keys!

reading: Clarice and Ethan meet at a grocery store. Clarice drops her keys, and Ethan returns them. Clarice lives near the store and works nearby. She designs clothes. Ethan works at the hospital as an anesthesiologist. They introduce themselves and talk about their jobs. This is their first meeting. Clarice thanks Ethan for his help.

questions.prompt: Where do Clarice and Ethan meet?

task: Write three questions about the characters’ routines. Add one polite instruction beginning with Please.

title: Making a connection

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Hello again! Are you taking a break?

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Yes. I am drinking coffee before work. Are you working today?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I am finishing a design at my studio.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Would you like to have dinner with me sometime?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes. I am saving your number now.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Great. I am checking my schedule. I will call you to arrange it.

reading: The day after their first meeting, Clarice and Ethan see each other again. Ethan is drinking coffee before work. Clarice is finishing a design at her studio that day. Ethan invites her to dinner, and she accepts. They exchange phone numbers. They do not choose a restaurant or a time yet. Ethan is checking his schedule before he calls her.
task: Describe what Clarice and Ethan are doing. Write two affirmative sentences, one negative sentence and one question.

title: A family Saturday

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: This garden looks lovely. Is that your book, Sara?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Yes. These cushions are for the playroom.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: There is a new plant beside the gate. I will water it.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: After lunch, let’s go to the store.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Is that Ethan over there?

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Yes. He is a friend of Charlene’s. Let’s say hello.

reading: On Saturday, Taylor, Evan and Sara spend the morning at home. Taylor enjoys the garden. Sara takes cushions to the playroom. Evan waters a new plant beside the gate. After lunch, they go to the store. They see Ethan there and say hello. Taylor knows him through Charlene, their friend. Taylor works as a chef; she does not work at Ethan’s hospital.

questions.prompt: What does Sara take to the playroom?
When do they go to the store?
Through whom does Taylor know Ethan?

task: Describe the family’s home using a, an, the, this, that, these and those.

title: Checking in

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Hello. I have a reservation under Denali Kumar.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Welcome. Your room is on the second floor, opposite the elevator.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Thank you. Is the restaurant downstairs?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, next to the lobby. Breakfast is from seven to ten.

dialogue.speaker: Denali
dialogue.text: Perfect. I am here for four nights.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Here is your key. Enjoy your visit to Chicago.

reading: This episode returns to Denali’s arrival in Chicago. She checks in at a hotel for four nights. Her room is on the second floor, opposite the elevator. The restaurant is downstairs, next to the lobby. Breakfast is from seven to ten. Denali takes her key and goes to her room. Her visit lasts five days, including the day she arrives and the day she leaves.

questions.prompt: How many nights will Denali stay?
Which floor is her room on?

task: Draw a simple hotel plan. Write four sentences about where the room, elevator, restaurant and lobby are.

title: A difficult day out
time: Back with the Thompsons, on Sunday

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: Our trip was not very relaxing, was it?

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: No. We waited a long time at the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: The lake looked beautiful, but the water was too cold for swimming.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.text: And the line for the restrooms was very long.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: We left the park at seven in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Next time, let’s check the information and arrive earlier.

reading: The Thompson family visited a park on Sunday. They waited at the entrance and then walked to the lake. The water was too cold, so they did not swim. Later, there was a long line for the restrooms. The family left at seven in the evening. They were tired. Taylor suggested checking the information and arriving earlier on their next visit.

questions.prompt: Where was there a long line?

task: Retell the trip in five sentences. Use at least two irregular past forms and one negative sentence.

title: A table for two

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Hello. I was checking your menu when I decided to call. Can I book a table for Saturday at eight?

dialogue.speaker: Luiggi
dialogue.text: Eight is fully booked. We have a table upstairs at eight thirty.

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: That works. A table for two, please.

dialogue.speaker: Luiggi
dialogue.text: Certainly. May I have your name?

dialogue.speaker: Ethan
dialogue.text: Ethan Plein. I was looking for a quiet place for dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Luiggi
dialogue.text: Your reservation at Al Dente is confirmed for Saturday at eight thirty.

reading: On Thursday, Ethan called Al Dente while he was planning his first date with Clarice. Luiggi answered the phone. Ethan asked for a table at eight, but that time was fully booked. Luiggi offered a table upstairs at eight thirty on Saturday. Ethan accepted. The reservation is for two people. The confirmed time is eight thirty, not eight.

questions.prompt: What is the confirmed dinner time?

task: Write two sentences combining past continuous and past simple about Ethan’s phone call.

title: One thing at a time

dialogue.speaker: Charlene
dialogue.text: You look worried. What is happening?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I have a design deadline on Friday and a date on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Charlene
dialogue.text: Which task needs your attention first?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: The design. Could you tell me how to organize the afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: Charlene
dialogue.text: Write a short list and start with the most urgent task. You can ask for help, can’t you?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes. A plan will help me enjoy Saturday.

reading: Clarice talks to Charlene, her friend and a nurse. Clarice has a design deadline on Friday. Her first dinner date with Ethan is on Saturday. Charlene asks her which task is most urgent. Clarice decides to finish the design first. Charlene suggests a short list and asking for help when needed. Clarice feels more organized after their conversation.
focus: WH questions, indirect questions and question tags
task: Ask Clarice one WH question, one polite indirect question and one question tag.

title: An evening together

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Is this your list of films or mine?

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: It is mine. I would like to watch a science-fiction film.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: I prefer a comedy. Can we choose one together?

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: Of course. And what about dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Let’s go to the Japanese restaurant. Their sushi is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Evan
dialogue.text: Good idea. The sashimi is my favorite. We can see the comedy afterward.

reading: Taylor and Evan plan an evening together. Evan’s list includes science-fiction films, but Taylor prefers a comedy. They agree to watch the comedy after dinner. They choose a Japanese restaurant. Taylor likes its sushi, and Evan likes the sashimi. They both help make the plan. The evening is for Taylor and Evan, not for Clarice and Ethan.

questions.prompt: Which type of film do they choose?
What kind of restaurant do they choose?
What is Evan’s favorite dish there?

task: Describe three possessions belonging to the characters. Use a possessive adjective, a possessive pronoun and apostrophe s.

title: Getting ready

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Will you help me choose something for tomorrow’s date?

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Of course. I will meet you at three.

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Thank you. Ethan will pick me up at seven forty-five tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: Will you wear the blue dress?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I think so. I will look for a simple bag to go with it.

dialogue.speaker: Taylor
dialogue.text: We will find one. You have already finished your design, haven’t you?

reading: On Friday, Clarice asks Taylor for help with her outfit. They agree to meet at three in the afternoon. The date is on Saturday. Ethan will pick Clarice up at seven forty-five, before their eight-thirty dinner reservation. Clarice plans to wear a blue dress and look for a simple bag. Her urgent design is finished, so she can enjoy the afternoon.

questions.prompt: When do Clarice and Taylor meet?
What time will Ethan pick Clarice up?

task: Make three offers or promises to help Clarice. Use will and write one question with Will you...?

title: A plan for tomorrow

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Caleb, my laptop is very slow. Are you going to check it today?

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: Yes. I am going to look at it this afternoon. Have you backed up your designs?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: Yes. They are in my backup folder.

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: Good. What are you going to do tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Clarice
dialogue.text: I am going to have dinner with Ethan at Al Dente.

dialogue.speaker: Caleb
dialogue.text: Enjoy it! I am going to call you when the laptop is ready.

reading: Clarice visits Caleb’s computer shop on Friday. Her laptop is slow. Caleb is going to check it that afternoon. Clarice has backed up her designs, so she has another copy of her work. She tells Caleb about her plan for Saturday: dinner with Ethan at Al Dente. Caleb is going to call when the laptop is ready. The dinner has not happened yet.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the laptop?

task: Write Clarice’s and Caleb’s plans using be going to. Explain the difference between a plan and a spontaneous offer.
